QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_59

question.text: What documentation must a hedger provide to claim higher position limits in ETIRD?

answer.text: Proof of underlying exposure such as details of bond holdings, loan obligations, or other interest rate exposure
No documentation is required; higher limits are automatic
A simple self-declaration letter is sufficient
Only a certificate from a chartered accountant

explanation.text: The Logic: Exchanges differentiate hedger position limits from speculative position limits because hedgers reduce, rather than add, market risk. To claim hedger treatment with higher allowable positions in Exchange Traded Interest Rate Derivatives (ETIRD), a participant must demonstrate that the futures/options position offsets an actual underlying interest-rate exposure — typically via bond holdings, loan obligations, or similar documented assets or liabilities sensitive to interest rates. The Trap: Higher limits are never granted automatically — that would defeat the purpose of position-limit policy. A self-declaration alone gives the exchange no verifiable proof. A standalone CA certificate, without the underlying-exposure evidence, is also insufficient. Note: The NISM-Series-IV Interest Rate Derivatives workbook (Dec 2025) sets out category-wise position limits and the general requirement that companies demonstrate hedging purpose, but pages 234-237, 286, and 329 do not specifically list bond holdings or loan obligations as the required documentation. The framing above is general exchange-practice knowledge.
